title: Redwood Migration Demo: OpenAI / Anthropic / Together -> Redwood
summary: Redwood AE/SE run a migration parity demo mapping BlueCrest's existing OpenAI/Anthropic/Together usage to Redwood API and Console. Focus on API parity, streaming, function/tool calling, cost comparisons, dedicated vs hosted, VPC options and benchmarks. Customer asks for pricing worksheet, security docs (SOC2/KMS), and an initial POC for classification pipeline. Agreed next steps: send pricing + security pack, schedule POC kick-off and perf benchmark window.
topics: API parity mapping (model names, params, tokens)
Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and VPC/private deployment
Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO
action_items: Alex Martinez: Send pricing worksheet and Dedicated capacity addendum by 2026-12-15
Priya Singh: Share benchmark plan + sample load script (k6) by 2026-12-14
Jonah Wu: Export Console screenshots & routing examples into slide deck by 2026-12-13
Evan Cho (BlueCrest): Provide dataset sample and expected QPS for benchmark by 2026-12-16
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing + security docs (SOC2, ISO excerpt, KMS guide)
Schedule 2-week POC start for classification pipeline (customer to confirm dates)
Run baseline throughput/latency benchmark vs OpenAI model (Redwood to propose test harness)
Follow-up call to review POC scope and success criteria week of 2026-12-21
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11 15:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jonah (Redwood Product), Sarah (BlueCrest CTO), Daniel (ML Eng), Priya R (Product), Evan (Security), Maya (SRE)

Summary section (auto): quick parity demo, mapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls to Redwood API endpoints; show Console + Optimize suggestions.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, uh thanks for carving out time, I'm Alex with Redwood, i'm the AE on this deal. Priya's gonna run the demo, Jonah will chime on Console questions.
[00:14] Sarah: Thanks Alex, excited — we want to see how close Redwood is to our current stack. We're currently on OpenAI for chat, Anthropic for safety checks, and Together for a subset of classification calls.
[00:29] Priya (SE): Great. Quick agenda: API parity mapping, streaming and function calling, Console walkthrough, Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization), and then Q&A. We'll leave 10 min for next steps.
[00:42] Daniel: Quick note — our critical constraints are sub-200ms tail latency for short responses, 200 req/s sustained for some endpoints, and enterprise data residency for audit logs.
[00:55] Priya (SE): Totally — we'll show both hosted and Dedicated options, and the private/VPC variants, and where you'd push each workload.
[01:12] [screen share starts] Priya: First: API call mapping. So your OpenAI calls like "gpt-4o-mini" map to our curated model "redwood/gpt-4o-mini-v1" — same param surface mostly: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop, and streaming works via chunked responses. Note: our function calling is compatible with typical function schema but we call it "tool calling" in Console.
[01:42] Daniel: How about the Anthropic safety guard checks? We have a pre-processing step that hits Anthropic for safety filter and then go to OpenAI.
[02:00] Priya (SE): You can keep that sequence; Redwood supports multi-route routing — you could route by policy: safety route (Anthropic or a Redwood-safety-smaller model) then generation route. Or collapse both to Redwood if you want a single vendor. There was a small stutter here, apologies, the notes show "Anthorpic" sometimes in our internal scripts.
[02:25] Alex: Important to call out that for parity there are two levers: model name mapping and runtime config — e.g., context window / kv cache behavior. Our KV cache is conservative by default but you can tune it — we sometimes see folks mishear that as K-V cash (laughs) in docs.
[02:44] Maya (SRE): For Dedicated, what's the on-prem story? We need private control plane options due to compliance.
[02:55] Jonah (Product): We offer a Private deployment with customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem package. Audit logs, KMS integrations (HSM possible) and RBAC are included. Evan, feel free to interrupt if you want security detail now.
[03:12] Evan (Security): Yeah, can you send SOC2 scope and KMS integration docs afterwards? Also interested in key rotation and HSM options.
[03:22] Jonah: Absolutely — we'll attach those in the follow-up.
[03:28] [demo continues] Priya (SE): Now streaming demo — I'll do a side-by-side. Left is OpenAI streaming call, right is Redwood stream using our SDK. You'll see chunked events with same tokens; small differences: Redwood batches low-latency traffic but keeps per-request latency low via priority routing.
[04:02] Daniel: Curious on batching — how do you keep latency under 200ms while batching?
[04:12] Priya: Good Q. We do continuous batching with priority lanes: small requests go to the low-latency lane, batching occurs within a small micro-window, and we fall back to dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput. We also use prefix/KV caching to avoid recomputing identical prefixes. That said, if you have many short-turn chats, the low-latency lane is what you want.
[04:45] Sarah: What's the typical token cost delta vs OpenAI? Our CFO will want a rough% estimate.
[04:55] Alex: We'll send a pricing worksheet but in our experience parity models on Redwood reduce per-token cost 10-40% depending on quantization and batching. For example customers who accept int8 quantization see ~30% token-cost drop with near-parity quality.
[05:12] Daniel: About Together models — some of our classifiers are on Together. Are those available?
[05:22] Priya: We host several Together-family models as curated entries; for parity we map their API params to ours and expose equivalent model ids. There can be small differences in tokenizer handling — we include migration notes and recommend running the tokenizer diff as part of POC.
[05:45] [timestamped transcript with small imperfections follows, occasional crosstalk]
[06:10] Priya: Now Console: Jonas — sorry Jonah — i'll flip to routing dashboard — here you can define per-route model pins, canary rollouts, automatic fallback (e.g., if Dedicated capacity is saturated, route to hosted cheaper model). You also get token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency percentiles and tracing hooks.
[06:40] Jonah: Also show the Optimize tab — we recommend batching/window sizes, quantization profiles per model, and flag potential regression checks against your eval set. You can pin a baseline evaluation and get alerts when quality drops.
[07:05] Priya R (BlueCrest Product): That eval feature sounds useful — we have a set of prompts where we track precision/recall. Can we upload our test set?
[07:17] Priya (SE): Yes, you can upload prompt sets and define assertion rules; we support both automated regression alerts and manual review workflows.
[07:30] [question about SSO and RBAC]
[07:40] Evan: SSO? We currently use Okta and need SCIM provisioning.
[07:45] Jonah: We support SAML + SCIM, roles-based RBAC and audit logs with retention controls.
[07:52] Sarah: Any weird gotchas on migration — tokens, stop sequences, or output formatting?
[07:59] Priya: There are small tokenizer differences, stop-sequence behavior can vary, and tool/function calling shape differences. Our migration checklist includes tokenizer diff, sample prompt A/B testing, and mapping function schema (we'll map Together/OpenAI function calls to Redwood tool calls). We usually recommend a short 2-week POC to validate quality and perf.
[08:25] Daniel: Perf — can you run a benchmark against our current OpenAI baseline? We can provide a dataset and expected QPS; interested mainly in tail latency and 95/99 percentiles.
[08:36] Priya: Yes — we'll propose a benchmark harness (we often use k6 + a small harness) and share scripts. We'll need a sample payload and goals.
[08:48] [small interruption, background noise for a sec]
[09:00] Alex: To summarize the Dedicated vs Hosted decision: if you need predictable tail latency and isolation, Dedicated reserved capacity is recommended; if you want lower ops and pay-as-you-go, hosted API is fine. Private (VPC) sits between with customer-managed networking and control plane isolation.
[09:25] Sarah: How long to spin Dedicated up if we sign?
[09:30] Jonah: Typical lead time 2-4 weeks depending on region and capacity; we'll include burst options during ramp.
[09:38] Daniel: On quantization — we've seen quality hit with int8 on some models. Does Redwood provide model-level recommendations?
[09:47] Priya: Yes Optimize will recommend quantization profile per workload. We also run small evals to validate quality delta and recommend mixed precision if necessary.
[10:05] [demo shows route definitions and a canary deploy flow]
[10:40] Priya (SE): One more note on logs/data retention: hosted keeps logs for configured retention; Dedicated/Private you control retention and can ship logs to your SIEM. Audit trails include token-level usage for cost attribution.
[11:05] Evan: For KMS — we need envelope encryption and HSM-backed keys for some customers.
[11:12] Jonah: Supported — we'll include HSM options in the security pack.
[11:20] [customer question] Priya R: In terms of SDKs — how much code change? Our engs use the OpenAI python client a lot.
[11:30] Priya (SE): We provide drop-in SDKs with helpers and a compatibility layer for common OpenAI call shapes; many customers change only the import and model string, and run a small adapter for function/tool calling differences. We will provide a migration guide with example diffs.
[11:55] Daniel: Any rate-limit or quota differences we should worry about during POC?
[12:02] Alex: For Hosted, there are tenant-level quotas we can set; for Dedicated you get reserved throughput. During POC we'll mirror your expected QPS.
[12:20] [closing part: recap & next steps]
[12:35] Alex: Okay wrap up — action items: we'll send pricing worksheet, security docs (SOC2, KMS, HSM notes), benchmark plan and sample harness, and a migration checklist. BlueCrest will send sample dataset and expected QPS. We'll target a POC window in the week of 2026-12-21 — is that workable?
[12:58] Sarah: Yes that's workable, i'll confirm with the team and Evan will provide security constraints.
[13:06] Daniel: Quick ask — can you include a cost projection comparing our current spend on OpenAI/Anthropic/Together vs Redwood hosted and Dedicated for our 200 QPS peak?
[13:15] Alex: Yes we'll include that in the pricing worksheet.
[13:20] [end of recording]
